title: RemoteEvent:FireClient()
summary: Server → one specific client. First argument is the target Player, followed by any serializable values. The client's OnClientEvent receives only the values (no player parameter).

parameters.name: ...args
parameters.description: Payload delivered to that client's OnClientEvent.

details.heading: Server-only
details.body: Clients cannot FireClient (not even to themselves through the remote). Client→server is FireServer.

explanation.whatItIs: A private server → player message: 'here is YOUR inventory / YOUR reward / a message just for you'.
explanation.whyItExists: Some information is per-player (personal stats, secret roles); broadcasting it leaks data and wastes bandwidth.
whenToUse: Per-player data delivery (shop contents for that player, trade offers)
Triggering client effects for one person (screen flash, sound)
Replies to a specific player's earlier FireServer
whenNotToUse: You need a return value — RemoteFunction:InvokeClient
tips: The target Player must still be connected — nil/leaving players just drop the message
Client receives exactly the ...args — no player prepended on this side
commonMistakes: Forgetting the player argument: FireClient("data") errors
Expecting other players to receive it
Sending to a player mid-leave and treating it as delivered

examples.title: Reply to one player
examples.code:
-- Server:
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, request)
    if request == "GetCoins" then
        local coins = getCoinsFor(player)   -- your server data
        remote:FireClient(player, "CoinsResult", coins)
    end
end)

-- Client:
remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(kind, value)
    if kind == "CoinsResult" then
        print("I have", value, "coins")
    end
end)
